issues.description: The return type for Farm.singFarmSong() (and its helper singFarmSongVerse) differs between the exercise specification/template and the provided solution. The UML and problem text require singFarmSong():void and instruct students to print the song (Problem statement UML shows + singFarmSong():void and the text at the task says “prints the Old MacDonald had a Farm song”). The template implementation declares public void singFarmSong() (template Farm.java line 9) and a private void singFarmSongVerse(...) (template Farm.java line 18). The solution implementation instead declares public String singFarmSong() (solution Farm.java line 59) and private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal) (solution Farm.java line 33). This divergence can confuse students about whether they should implement printing directly (void) or return a String, and it may affect automated tests or grading expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferred to match the problem text and template): change the solution so Farm.singFarmSong() is declared as void and performs printing to System.out (and adjust or keep a String-returning helper but ensure the public method prints). Also change singFarmSongVerse in the solution to a void helper that prints the verse or make the public method call and print the helper's returned String. Option B (if returning String is intentional): update the UML and problem text to specify singFarmSong():String and document that the returned String must be printed by callers or by tests. Apply the same decision to the helper method (singFarmSongVerse) so both template, spec, and solution agree.
